import json

from lfx.custom.custom_component.component import Component
from lfx.io import MultilineInput, Output
from lfx.schema.data import Data


class WebhookComponent(Component):
    display_name = "Webhook"
    documentation: str = "https://docs.langflow.org/component-webhook"
    name = "Webhook"
    icon = "webhook"

    inputs = [
        MultilineInput(
            name="data", display_name="Payload",
            info="Receives a payload from external systems via HTTP POST.",
            advanced=True,
        ),
        MultilineInput(
            name="curl", display_name="cURL", value="CURL_WEBHOOK",
            advanced=True, input_types=[],
        ),
        MultilineInput(
            name="endpoint", display_name="Endpoint", value="BACKEND_URL",
            advanced=False, copy_field=True, input_types=[],
        ),
    ]
    outputs = [
        Output(display_name="JSON", name="output_data", method="build_data"),
    ]

    def build_data(self) -> Data:
        if not self.data:
            self.status = "No data provided."
            return Data(data={})
        try:
            # Permit literal control characters inside JSON strings, including
            # multiline email previews. Do not rewrite or remove email text.
            body = json.loads(self.data, strict=False)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
            self.status = "Invalid JSON payload."
            raise ValueError(
                f"Webhook payload is invalid JSON at line {exc.lineno}, "
                f"column {exc.colno}: {exc.msg}"
            ) from exc
        if not isinstance(body, dict):
            raise ValueError("Webhook payload must be a JSON object.")
        data = Data(data=body)
        self.status = data
        return data

from lfx.base.models.model import LCModelComponent
from lfx.base.models.unified_models import (
    get_language_model_options,
    get_llm,
    handle_model_input_update,
)
from lfx.base.models.watsonx_constants import IBM_WATSONX_URLS
from lfx.components.models_and_agents.model_selection import apply_model_overrides
from lfx.field_typing.constants import LanguageModel
from lfx.field_typing.range_spec import RangeSpec
from lfx.inputs.inputs import BoolInput, DropdownInput, StrInput
from lfx.io import IntInput, MessageInput, ModelInput, MultilineInput, SecretStrInput, SliderInput


class LanguageModelComponent(LCModelComponent):
    display_name = "Email Intent Check LLM"
    description = "Runs a language model given a specified provider."
    documentation: str = "https://docs.langflow.org/components-models"
    icon = "brain-circuit"
    category = "models"

    inputs = [
        ModelInput(
            name="model",
            display_name="Language Model",
            info="Select your model provider",
            real_time_refresh=True,
            required=True,
        ),
        StrInput(
            name="model_name",
            display_name="Model Name Override",
            info=(
                "Optional model name to use instead of the selected model. "
                "Can be set from a global variable for runtime model selection."
            ),
            advanced=True,
            load_from_db=False,
        ),
        StrInput(
            name="provider",
            display_name="Provider Override",
            info=(
                "Optional provider to use with Model Name Override. Leave blank to use the selected model's provider."
            ),
            advanced=True,
            load_from_db=False,
        ),
        SecretStrInput(
            name="api_key",
            display_name="API Key",
            info="Overrides global provider settings. Leave blank to use your pre-configured API Key.",
            required=False,
            show=True,
            real_time_refresh=True,
            advanced=True,
        ),
        DropdownInput(
            name="base_url_ibm_watsonx",
            display_name="watsonx API Endpoint",
            info="The base URL of the API (IBM watsonx.ai only)",
            options=IBM_WATSONX_URLS,
            value=IBM_WATSONX_URLS[0],
            combobox=True,
            show=False,
            real_time_refresh=True,
        ),
        StrInput(
            name="project_id",
            display_name="watsonx Project ID",
            info="The project ID associated with the foundation model (IBM watsonx.ai only)",
            show=False,
            required=False,
        ),
        StrInput(
            name="ollama_base_url",
            display_name="Ollama API URL",
            info="Endpoint of the Ollama API (Ollama only)",
            show=False,
            real_time_refresh=True,
        ),
        MessageInput(
            name="input_value",
            display_name="Input",
            info="The input text to send to the model",
        ),
        MultilineInput(
            name="system_message",
            display_name="System Message",
            info="A system message that helps set the behavior of the assistant",
            advanced=False,
        ),
        BoolInput(
            name="stream",
            display_name="Stream",
            info="Whether to stream the response",
            value=False,
            advanced=True,
        ),
        SliderInput(
            name="temperature",
            display_name="Temperature",
            value=0.1,
            info="Controls randomness in responses",
            range_spec=RangeSpec(min=0, max=1, step=0.01),
            advanced=True,
        ),
        IntInput(
            name="max_tokens",
            display_name="Max Tokens",
            info="Maximum number of tokens to generate. Field name varies by provider.",
            advanced=True,
            range_spec=RangeSpec(min=1, max=128000, step=1, step_type="int"),
        ),
    ]

    def build_model(self) -> LanguageModel:
        model = apply_model_overrides(
            self.model,
            model_name=getattr(self, "model_name", None),
            provider=getattr(self, "provider", None),
            user_id=self.user_id,
            get_options=get_language_model_options,
        )
        return get_llm(
            model=model,
            user_id=self.user_id,
            api_key=self.api_key,
            temperature=self.temperature,
            stream=self.stream,
            max_tokens=getattr(self, "max_tokens", None),
            watsonx_url=getattr(self, "base_url_ibm_watsonx", None),
            watsonx_project_id=getattr(self, "project_id", None),
            ollama_base_url=getattr(self, "ollama_base_url", None),
        )

    def update_build_config(self, build_config: dict, field_value: str, field_name: str | None = None):
        """Dynamically update build config with user-filtered model options."""
        return handle_model_input_update(self, build_config, field_value, field_name)

# Role

You are an AI Email Understanding Agent for an NBFC customer-support workflow.

You receive:
- `current_email`
- `thread`
- `thread_metadata`

Thread messages may have these directions:
- `INBOUND`
- `OUTBOUND_SUPPORT`
- `CURRENT_INBOUND`

Your job is to:
1. Understand the customer's current business intent.
2. Identify unresolved requests or questions.
3. Assess tone, urgency, and escalation need.
4. Extract identifiers explicitly mentioned in the thread.

Do not answer the customer.
Do not retrieve external information.
Do not invent or infer missing facts or identifiers.

# Output

Return only valid JSON in this exact structure:

{
  "primary_intent": "",
  "secondary_intents": [],
  "latest_customer_request": "",
  "unresolved_questions": [],
  "tone": "",
  "urgency": "",
  "escalation_required": false,
  "identifiers": {
    "customer_id": null,
    "loan_id": null,
    "application_id": null,
    "transaction_reference": null,
    "other_identifiers": []
  },
  "identifier_conflicts": [],
  "reason": ""
}

# Intent Rules

- Give highest priority to `CURRENT_INBOUND`.
- Use the full thread to understand short or context-dependent follow-ups.
- Identify the underlying business issue, not generic labels such as "follow-up" or "update".
- `primary_intent` must be a concise uppercase business intent.
- `secondary_intents` should contain only additional active requests.
- `latest_customer_request` should describe what the customer currently wants in one concise sentence.
- `unresolved_questions` should contain only issues that remain unresolved after considering both customer and support messages.
- A support acknowledgement or promise is not a resolution unless the actual issue was resolved.

# Tone and Urgency

`tone` must be one of:
- `NEUTRAL`
- `POLITE`
- `CONCERNED`
- `FRUSTRATED`
- `ANGRY`

`urgency` must be one of:
- `LOW`
- `NORMAL`
- `HIGH`
- `CRITICAL`

Assess tone primarily from `CURRENT_INBOUND`, using the thread as context.

Set `escalation_required` to `true` when there are repeated unresolved follow-ups, strong dissatisfaction, missed support commitments, explicit escalation requests, or another clear reason for human attention.

Do not mark something `CRITICAL` based only on an angry tone.

# Identifier Extraction

Extract identifiers from the full thread only when explicitly present.

Supported fields:
- `customer_id`
- `loan_id`
- `application_id`
- `transaction_reference`

Use `other_identifiers` only for relevant identifiers that do not fit these fields:

{
  "type": "",
  "value": ""
}

### Identifier precedence:
- Consider the chronological thread context.
- If an earlier identifier was explicitly rejected, corrected, replaced, or superseded
  later in the thread, use the latest explicitly supplied replacement value.
- Do NOT treat superseded identifiers as conflicts.
- Use identifier_conflicts only when multiple values remain simultaneously unresolved and there is no clear correction or replacement in the conversation.

## Mapping Rules

- `customer_id`: customer ID, customer number, customer code, cust ID, or "my ID" when referring to the customer's identity/account.
- `loan_id`: loan ID, loan number, loan account number.
- `application_id`: application ID, application number.
- `transaction_reference`: transaction ID, transaction number, transaction reference, txn ID, txn ref, payment reference, payment ID, UTR, or bank reference.

Prefer the explicit label used by the customer over contextual inference.

Do not guess, reconstruct, or infer identifiers.

If the same identifier appears repeatedly with the same value, return it once.

If conflicting values appear for the same identifier type:
- return `null` for that field
- record the conflict as:

{
  "type": "",
  "values": []
}

Do not extract the customer's email address from message body text. Sender email is handled separately from trusted metadata.

# General Rules

- Use thread context only to interpret the current issue.
- Do not treat quoted or repeated historical text as a new request.
- Do not invent missing history.
- Keep all text fields concise.
- Return only the JSON object with no markdown, commentary, or code fences.

from lfx.custom.custom_component.component import Component
from lfx.io import DataInput, Output
from lfx.schema.data import Data


class DemoSendOutcome(Component):
    display_name = "5. Send Reply & Record Outcome"
    description = "Sends the approved response and records the final outcome."
    icon = "send"
    name = "DemoSendOutcome"

    inputs = [
        DataInput(
            name="review_result",
            display_name="Approved Response",
            required=True,
        ),
    ]

    outputs = [
        Output(
            name="outcome",
            display_name="Outcome",
            method="build_result",
        ),
    ]

    def build_result(self) -> Data:
        value = self.review_result
        if isinstance(value, Data):
            value = value.data
        return Data(data={"status": "sent", "review_result": value})
